description:
I am Dr Manu Mohan, MD (Preventive Medicine), Major, Army Medical Corps. I specialise in digital epidemiology, AI-enabled disease surveillance, causal inference, and environmental determinants of health.

Our focus is the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge. We will select NASA Earth-system variables, quantify long-term trends, test statistical significance, and convert the strongest signals into actionable early-warning insights for population health
summary:
I work in preventive medicine, where a surveillance signal should tell us where to look next. I built Astra XYZ to bring that way of thinking to NASA Earth data. The tool lets users explore 33 years of air temperature, relative humidity, and surface soil wetness across five locations in Ghana using NASA POWER data.

Users can compare locations, switch between annual means and baseline anomalies, and see the direction, rate, and uncertainty of each trend. In Accra, mean air temperature rose by 0.17 °C per decade, with a nominal 95% confidence interval of 0.13 to 0.20 °C per decade. Accra was the only location where both adjusted temperature trend tests flagged a change.

For a public health team, that is a starting point for investigation. The next step is to compare these environmental signals with local weather, mosquito surveillance, and confirmed cases before setting any threshold for action.
details:
In preventive medicine, the first question a surveillance signal should answer is where should we look more closely? I built Astra XYZ to ask that question of NASA Earth data. The interactive tool lets users explore 33 years of air temperature, relative humidity, and surface soil wetness at five locations in Ghana using NASA POWER data from 1991 to 2023.

Users select a variable and location, then switch between annual values and departures from the 1991–2007 baseline. Sen’s slope estimates the change per decade, with a nominal 95% confidence interval. An annual Mann–Kendall test assesses the trend, and a Newey–West trend t-test checks how sensitive the result is to serial dependence. We adjusted for 15 comparisons and flagged a trend only when both tests met the significance criterion and the slopes agreed in direction. In Accra, air temperature rose by 0.17 °C per decade, with a nominal 95% confidence interval of 0.13 to 0.20 °C. It was the only location where both adjusted temperature tests flagged a trend.

The creative step was to treat environmental trends as leads for public health surveillance. A district team could use a flagged location to decide where to review local weather records, mosquito surveillance, and confirmed cases together. We considered seasonal variation, correlation between successive years, multiple comparisons, and the limits of interpreting five model grid locations. Disease forecasting would require local outcome data and validation before setting thresholds for action.

We used Python, NumPy, and SciPy for the analysis and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the browser-based explorer. The project runs on a standard computer and includes the original NASA data, analysis code, and downloadable results so others can check and reproduce the findings.
